instructions: Cut each chicken thigh in half. Pat the pieces dry and season them with 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper.
Core the peppers and cut them into 1 1/2 inch squares. Slice the garlic thin. Chop the pancetta.
Warm the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pancetta and cook for 3 minutes, until the fat runs and the edges turn lightly golden.
Add the chicken in a single layer. Leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is deep golden, then flip and cook for 3 minutes. It won't be cooked through yet. Transfer it to a plate.
Add the peppers to the skillet and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells sweet.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with their juice and crush them with the back of a spoon. Add the broth and the rest of the salt and pepper. Return the chicken and any juices from the plate.

Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to medium-low and partly cover. Simmer for 15 minutes, until the peppers are soft and the sauce clings to the chicken. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into a thick piece: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve in shallow bowls with the sauce spooned over.
method_notes: The Roman versions agree on chicken braised with peppers, garlic, white wine and tomato. The lead adds pancetta and broth; the others use fresh tomatoes or tomato paste instead. The lead uses jointed bone-in chicken simmered for 40 minutes; boneless thighs cut in half cook in 15 minutes here, which keeps it under 50. None of the three pages had ratings.
